text:
sam: quick checkin — ran a batch of profiling runs for MQA on Ampere nodes, and KV-cache page/block layout seems to flip which kernel wins around seq_len=384 :eyes:
anya: can you paste the commands / perf output? curious about the cross-over point
mike: if KV pages are 64k vs 128k that could change memory access patterns a lot; worth adding to the autotuner graph
sam: paste of the run (simplified):
```
# run: mqa-profile --model redwood-7b-mqa --batch 8 --seq_lens 64,128,256,384,512 --kv-page 64k --kv-block 256
# kernels: gqa_paged_attn_v1, mqa_blocked_attn_opt, gv_kv_layout_fused
seq=64  tokens/s: 11800  kernel: gqa_paged_attn_v1
seq=128 tokens/s: 7800   kernel: gqa_paged_attn_v1
seq=256 tokens/s: 4700   kernel: mqa_blocked_attn_opt
seq=384 tokens/s: 3600   kernel: mqa_blocked_attn_opt
seq=512 tokens/s: 2200   kernel: gv_kv_layout_fused
```
sam: when I flipped kv-page to 128k the crossover moved down to ~200-256
anya: so page size affects which kernel has better locality for MQA per-head scatter/gather, makes sense
julia: are these single-stream microbenchmarks or realistic conversational traces? we need distribution tests for batching heuristic tuning
sam: these are synthetic fixed-len runs. I also ran a distribution sample (500 traces from prod-sim): median_seq=180, p90=420, p99=900
mike: ok that distribution explains why the autotuner currently picks gqa for many requests but we still see edge latency spikes at p90 when kernels flip
anya: suggestion: add a feature in the kernel selector: (seq_len_bucket, kv_page_size, effective_heads) -> expected_throughput, learned from short A/B probes. keeps decision simple and cheap
sam: rough pseudo for selector scoring:
```
score = alpha * predicted_tput(seq, page, heads) - beta * tail_latency_penalty(seq)
if score_diff < margin: prefer lower-memory-path
```
mike: also consider keeping a shadow probe pool that runs an alternate kernel on a small fraction (0.5%) of requests to detect regressions post-deploy
julia: +1 on probes. add telemetry: kernel, seq_len_bucket, kv_page, tokens_generated, latency_ms. we can surface a drift alert in Console if alternate kernel crosses 10% perf regression
sam: another micro finding: blocked attn kernel benefits when kv-block is divisible by 256; we saw a ~8% boost when block aligned to 256 vs 192
anya: that suggests our autotuner should consider block_size candidate set aligned to hardware warp sizes and head-group tiling
perf-bot: perf-alert: nightly autotune jobs flagged 3 regressions for mqa_blocked_attn_opt on 1777776900..1777777000 window
mike: i'll dig into the CI artifacts. maybe a driver update changed shared mem scheduling causing less coalesced writes
sam: note: when enabling prefix cache reuse (kv-cache reuse across requests) the favored kernel sometimes changes because KV reuse reduces memory pressure — selector needs a flag for "cache_reuse=true"
anya: agreed. final proposed selector inputs: seq_len_bucket, batch_size_estimate, kv_page_size, kv_block_size, cache_reuse, effective_heads, hw_arch (A100/V100/Grace), model_variant (GQA/MQA)
julia: ops question — can the rollout be gradual? we should implement canary for selector model with 1% traffic ramp and automatic rollback if tail latency regresses >5%
sam: milestone: i'll implement a quick eval harness that sweeps kv_page {64k,128k}, kv_block {192,256,320}, seq_bins {<=128,129-256,257-512,>512} and logs best kernel per bucket. target PR by EOD Friday
anya: will add probe harness integration and telemetry schema
mike: i'll check driver/kernel matrix and add hardware-specific knobs
julia: i'll add a Console alert and a dashboard tile for kernel picks by bucket
sam: thanks team, will post results in this thread when sweep finishes :thumbsup:
